data.title: Pediculosis — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pediculosis** (Infestations)_

**Q1. Types of lice affecting humans?**
- Pediculus humanus capitis (head louse), Pediculus humanus corporis (body louse), Phthirus pubis (crab/pubic louse)

**Q2. Life cycle of the head louse?**
- Eggs (nits) cemented to hair shaft near scalp, hatch in 7–10 days into nymphs, mature in 9–12 days; adult female lays ~5–10 eggs/day and lives ~30 days; obligate blood feeders, die within 1–2 days off host

**Q3. Clinical features of pediculosis capitis?**
- Itching (occipital and post-auricular), nits on hair, live lice, excoriations, secondary impetigo, occipital lymphadenopathy, 'plica polonica' (matted hair) in neglected cases

**Q4. Nits vs pseudonits?**
- Nits are firmly cemented and cannot be slid along the hair; pseudonits (hair casts, dandruff, hair spray, piedra) move freely along the shaft

**Q5. Head louse vs body louse?**
- Body louse lives in clothing seams, lays eggs on fibres, causes vagabond's disease (hyperpigmented lichenified skin in neglected/homeless), transmits epidemic typhus (Rickettsia prowazekii), trench fever (Bartonella quintana), relapsing fever (Borrelia recurrentis)
- Head louse is not an important disease vector

**Q6. What is maculae caeruleae?**
- Slate-blue macules on thighs/trunk at sites of pubic louse feeding (altered haemoglobin from louse saliva)

**Q7. Treatment of head lice?**
- Permethrin 1% creme rinse 10 min, repeat on day 9–10; malathion 0.5%; ivermectin 0.5% lotion; spinosad 0.9%; dimeticone 4% (physical, no resistance); benzyl alcohol 5%
- Oral ivermectin 200–400 µg/kg on days 1 and 8 for resistance
- Wet combing with fine-tooth comb; treat contacts; wash bedding/combs in hot water

**Q8. Treatment of phthiriasis palpebrarum?**
- Petrolatum applied twice daily for 10 days (smothers lice), mechanical removal, oral ivermectin; pubic lice — evaluate for other STIs, treat partner

**Q9. What is pediculicide resistance?**
- Knockdown resistance (kdr) — sodium channel mutations reducing permethrin/pyrethrin efficacy; suspect if live lice persist after correct use

## Quick spotter facts
- Nits firmly attached to hair shafts with occipital excoriations — pediculosis capitis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Pediculosis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.22. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
